summary: There are four kinds of shomrim: an unpaid watchman, a borrower, a paid watchman, and a renter. Each one has different rules about paying when something happens to the item.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of watchmen:
chunks.st: There are four types of bailees, to whom different halakhot apply.

words.note: A shomer watches something that belongs to someone else.

chunks.en: an unpaid watchman,
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee, who receives no compensation for safeguarding the item in his care;

chunks.en: a borrower, a paid watchman,
chunks.st: and a borrower, who receives an item on loan for his own use without paying a rental fee; a paid bailee, who is paid a salary for safeguarding the deposited item;

chunks.en: and a renter.
chunks.st: and a renter, i.e., one who pays a fee for the use of an item or animal.
chunks.stMore: In the event that one of these bailees is unable to return the deposited item to its owner, the halakha with regard to liability is dependent upon what happened to the item, and upon the type of bailee:

chunks.en: An unpaid watchman swears, and then he is patur for everything.
chunks.st: An unpaid bailee takes an oath attesting to the fact that he was not negligent with the care of the item and is then exempt from liability for everything,
chunks.stMore: meaning for all types of damage, whether the item was lost, stolen, damaged, or if the animal died.

chunks.en: A borrower pays for everything.
chunks.st: Conversely, a borrower does not have the option of taking an oath, and pays for everything,
chunks.stMore: whether the item was stolen, lost, damaged, or the animal died, even if it was by unavoidable accident.

chunks.en: A paid watchman and a renter swear about
chunks.st: The halakhot of a paid bailee and a renter are the same: They take an oath concerning

chunks.en: an animal that was hurt, or captured, or died,
chunks.st: an injured animal, and concerning a captured one, and concerning a dead
chunks.stMore: animal, attesting to the fact that these mishaps were not caused by negligence, but rather by unavoidable accident, and then are exempt from liability.

chunks.en: and they pay if it was lost or stolen.
chunks.st: But they must pay if the deposit cannot be returned due to loss or theft, even if these were not caused by negligence.
